Finish schedule template

A finish schedule answers a spatial question: which treatment applies to which surface? It connects room and surface references to a defined finish, without pretending that every material quantity is already known.

What each field records

Room
Name the room consistently.
Surface
Specify floor, wall face, ceiling, or another identifiable surface.
Finish reference
Match the material register and relevant drawing.
Finish
Name retained conditions as well as new treatments.
Quantity
Leave an unmeasured surface blank.
Unit
State the measured or counted unit.
Preparation / condition
Record what needs survey or specialist assessment.
Status
Record the review state.
Drawing / note
Link the application to a current document.

How to use this template

Record each surface separately when treatments or preparation differ. The Window Room’s 20 m² is a nominal floor footprint, not a wall area, coverage calculation, or purchasing quantity. Verify substrate condition and product requirements independently.

  1. List room surfaces and exceptions.
  2. Assign finish references and link to approved product information when available.
  3. Review quantities, substrate conditions, and drawing consistency before preparing procurement information.

Review before use

  • Do not substitute floor area for wall area.
  • Do not assume one wall treatment applies to every wall face.
  • Do not invent waste factors or coverage rates without product and project information.
